title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting (from the previous page): S is a base scheme, M is a rank-2 vector bundle on S, G = GL(M) (identified with GL(2)_S) and PG = G/G_m. Grothendieck is checking a claim he had used several times: that p: G -> PG induces a bijection (43) between regular unipotent sections of G and those of PG. Surjectivity holds by definition, since a regular unipotent section of PG is one that is fppf-locally induced from G. So only injectivity needs checking. Suppose ε and λε are both regular unipotent, with λ a unit on S. Taking determinants gives (44) λ^2 = 1. Taking traces gives (45) 2λ = 2. Together these are necessary and sufficient for λε to be unipotent again, and then it is automatically regular. If 2 is invertible on S they force λ = 1. They do not in general, e.g. in characteristic 2 or over a non-reduced base. Writing λ = 1+ν turns them into (46) 2ν = 0, ν^2 = 0. Hence (43) is injective over S iff the only section of O_S with 2ν = 0 and ν^2 = 0 is ν = 0. He then names μ_2' ⊂ μ_2 (written as a double-struck letter with index 2, transcribed as ℍ_2) the closed subgroup scheme defined by (44)+(45). It is Spec Z[T]/(T^2-1, 2T-2), which equals Spec Z[S]/(S^2, 2S) via T = 1+S, i.e. Spec(Z ⊕ Z/2Z) with Z/2 an ideal of square zero (the 'dual numbers over Z relative to the module Z/2Z'). It is closed under multiplication and inversion, so it is a subgroup scheme. Over Q it is trivial; over F_2 it is the infinitesimal μ_2. On the next page this leads to the statement that μ'_{2,S} acts freely on the scheme of regular unipotents of G, with quotient Unip.rég(PG). He then confronts this with the bijection of Borels, B ↦ B/G_m, and of unipotent one-parameter subgroups, and suspects that the vertical maps 'regular unipotent -> one-parameter subgroup' fail to be injective when 2 is not invertible. Purpose: careful scheme-theoretic bookkeeping of forms of GL2/PGL2 over arbitrary bases, including Spec Z, in the 'loop equation' study, where elements ρ, σ, ε_0, ε_1 of GL2 attached to the modular-group presentation are being analysed.
errors: He calls μ_2' 'plat sur Z', but Z[S]/(S^2,2S) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/2Z has 2-torsion, so it is not flat over Z. It is finite over Z; its generic fibre is the trivial group and its fibre at 2 is μ_2 of order 2, so the fibre degree jumps. Consequently 'quotient by μ'_2' on the next page cannot be an fppf quotient by a flat group in the usual sense.
'Infinitesimal absolu' is only loosely correct: the group is trivial over Z[1/2] and infinitesimal at 2. It is not an infinitesimal flat group scheme over Z.

ideas.what: Injectivity of regular unipotents of GL2 -> PGL2 tested via det and trace: λ^2 = 1 and 2λ = 2, i.e. ν^2 = 0 and 2ν = 0
ideas.modern_name: Non-injectivity of the unipotent variety map under the central isogeny in characteristic 2 (μ_2 infinitesimal); behaviour of the unipotent scheme under non-étale centre
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group-scheme folklore (SGA3 circle; Springer–Steinberg on unipotent varieties in bad characteristic)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA3 (central isogenies, μ_n); this specific computation is not known to be published

ideas.what: Closed subgroup scheme μ_2' = Spec Z[S]/(S^2,2S) ⊂ μ_2, the 'dual numbers of Z relative to the module Z/2'
ideas.modern_name: Non-flat closed subgroup scheme of μ_2 over Z (identity section plus the fibre at 2); trivial square-zero extension Z ⊕ Z/2

ideas.what: Comparison of regular unipotents with Borels and unipotent one-parameter subgroups (B = Norm(B_u)) for G and PG over arbitrary S
ideas.modern_name: Regular unipotent elements and Borel subgroups over a general base (SGA3 Exp. XXII-type statements)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Demazure–Grothendieck SGA3; Steinberg/Springer for regular unipotents
ideas.where_published: SGA3 (Borel subgroups over a base); regular-unipotent facts not specifically there

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine self-check of a scheme-theoretic detail (regular unipotents of GL2 versus PGL2 at the prime 2), with a small slip claiming flatness. The characteristic-2 phenomenon is well known, and nothing here seems new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The group-scheme symbol rendered ℍ_2 / ℍ_2' is almost certainly Grothendieck's notation for μ_2 (written as a double-struck M-like letter); the next page writes M'_{2,S}.
'isomorphe en opérateur' is probably 'isomorphe au spectre' (i.e. μ_2' ≅ Spec of Z[T]/(T^2-1,2T-2)).
The insertion read as '{+étant+}' above 'unipot.' appears to be 'stricts' or similar ('soit encore strict. unipotent'), uncertain.
The equation 2ν=0, ν^2=0 is numbered (46) in the text that follows, consistent with the reference '(46)'.
'sous-schéma {+en groupes+} de ℍ_2 défini par (45)' should be understood as defined by (44) and (45) together.
